## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_inventory` must not retry beyond the project's 3-attempt cap. The rule that sets the cap stays in force, and this pull request adds the only exemption, so the exemption cannot justify the 8-attempt loop.

## Changes
This pull request adds `app/legacy/fetch.py`, which retries a legacy inventory fetch up to 8 times, and `app/health.py`, which retries a health probe up to 3 times. It also adds parametrized tests for both and a sentence to `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap fetch_inventory retries at 3 attempts — When the legacy service is down, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts. That breaks "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (docs/review-rules.md:5). The exemption at docs/review-rules.md:7 is a line this pull request adds, so it is reviewed as a change and does not count as a rule. — During an outage, each call can hold a worker thread for about 87 seconds (8 × 10 s timeout plus 7 × 1 s delay), which is the failure docs/review-rules.md:6 describes. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3`, update the `fetch` case in `CASES` at tests/test_retries.py:10, and remove the exemption added at docs/review-rules.md:7. If the nightly restart needs longer coverage, use a longer delay within 3 attempts.
